Full blizzard: thousands of individual white specks crowd the water so thickly the far rooftops dissolve into pale grey, each flake a separate soft point catching the warm amber light from the left side while the right sinks into deep blue shadow.

Last few flakes after the storm: seven or eight large lazy specks drift alone through water that is nearly clear, each one a distinct rounded flake tumbling end-over-end in slow motion, amber window-light from the little house below throwing a warm halo up around each passing one.

Snow rising: hundreds of fine white specks are moving upward off the rooftop ridges, each a tiny bright point lit from below by cold blue light bouncing off the settled white drifts, the dark water above them still and waiting to receive them back.

One enormous slow flake close to the glass, soft and faintly translucent, drifting down a full hand's-width ahead of a loose haze of much smaller specks far behind it, the near flake lit vivid warm gold while the distant haze stays cool and blue.

One whole side of the water is packed with hundreds of dense white specks crowding together, each still individually visible as a separate soft point, while the far side of the water holds only clear deep indigo, the boundary between them ragged and shifting.

Warm grey ash instead of snow: hundreds of soft irregular specks in pale charcoal and warm taupe drift slowly downward, each one catching a dim orange glow from a lit window below, settling into a fine grey ridge along the ridgeline of every roof.

Drifting pollen and dandelion seed: each suspended particle a tiny gold filament, dozens of them hanging nearly still at different depths in the water, the light coming in warm and amber from one side and igniting each filament into a thread of bright yellow against the deep green water behind.

Cherry petals turning as they fall: each a broad flat blush-pink petal rotating slowly on its own axis as it descends, the water catching them spread wide and face-on so the warm rose colour shows fully, lit from above in cold white that makes the pink saturate to almost red at the edges.

Fine silt and rising bubbles through a reef: hundreds of pale cream silt specks drifting upward alongside dozens of small distinct spherical bubbles, each bubble carrying a bright white highlight on its upper-left face and a shadow of deep teal beneath, the water itself thick and slow around them.

Grey moon dust hanging in perfectly still water: hundreds of fine pale silver-grey specks suspended absolutely still at every depth, each one holding its exact place, the cold blue light from directly above pressing down onto each speck and leaving the water between them an even, undisturbed deep navy.

Rain: thousands of short bright streaks, each one a distinct straight line of refracting white light about three millimetres long, all of them slanting left at the same angle through deep blue-grey water, the low amber light catching the top end of each streak and leaving the bottom end dark.

Golden sparks lifting off a bonfire: dozens of individual bright amber specks rising in a loose upward scatter, each one a separate warm orange point, the lowest ones lit most intensely in deep gold while the higher ones cool toward pale yellow against the dark brown water above the fire's glow.

Bright green flecks of aurora light suspended in the water itself: each a small rounded point of clear vivid green at a different depth and position, none of them moving, the cold deep blue of the surrounding water making each green point read as something close to electric, the whole field of them spread unevenly across the upper half.

Thirty or forty distinct spherical bubbles rising one behind another, each with a sharp white highlight and a deep teal shadow, all of them rising but angled fifteen degrees off vertical as though the world beneath them leans, the warm amber light from the lower left catching each sphere on its belly.

Sand drifting warm and brown over a caravan route: hundreds of individual specks in burnt sienna and pale ochre rolling slowly forward along the bottom of the water, each speck distinct and tumbling, the low warm orange light from the right side casting a long shadow behind every grain across the pale sandy bed below.

Confetti over a carnival: dozens of small flat specks in saturated cobalt, deep red, and bright yellow, each one a separate bright round scrap catching the warm white light from above on its flat face and flashing a different vivid colour as it rotates slowly downward through clear water.

Fireflies instead of flakes: forty or fifty individual warm amber pinpoints distributed through the dark water at irregular depths, none of them touching, each a distinct physical speck with a brighter core and a slightly softer edge, the surrounding water deep enough in blue-black to make each point read as its own small source of warmth.

Soap-bubble iridescence in the water where the light hits the surface tension low down: a dozen thin-walled spheres of different sizes drifting upward, each one showing a distinct band of deep violet along one edge and pale green along the opposite edge, the bands shifting position as each bubble rotates slowly in the warm side-light.

Snow with a fresh spin to it, the whole field of individual white specks moving in a wide slow arc as though the world was set down only a moment ago and the water still remembers the rotation, each speck a distinct soft point, the warm gold light catching the outermost ring of the spiral more brightly than the dark centre.

The tail end of a blizzard thinning out: the lower third of the water still holds hundreds of crowded white specks, each one distinct, but above them the specks grow fewer and more spread until the top of the water holds only cold blue depth and a dozen slow isolated flakes making their way down alone.

Snow packed against one side by a heavy invisible wind, each of the hundreds of individual white specks pressed close to the right edge of the water and moving rightward together at a low slant, the left side of the water deep and open in cool indigo, the warm amber light catching every speck on its left face as it travels.

Fine mist of ice crystals so small each one is only a single point of white, tens of thousands of them distributed through the full depth of the water, the cold blue light from above catching them across the whole upper half while the lower half glows faint amber from the lit windows of the world beneath, the surface of that world wavering slightly through the dense suspension.

Autumn leaves scaled down to specks: each a separate flat oval in deep ochre or burnt orange rotating slowly as it sinks, the warm side-light catching the upper face of each leaf-speck and leaving the underside in shadow so every one reads as a distinct three-dimensional object falling through the slow thick water.

A drift of tiny white specks collecting in a soft uneven ridge along the rooftop peak below, while above them the rest of the individual specks are still in motion, the settled layer at the bottom lit by cold blue from above pressing the white into bright relief against the dark wet surface of the roof beneath.

Bioluminescent plankton scaled to specks: hundreds of individual points in cold vivid cyan scattered through deep water the colour of midnight blue, each point a separate physical speck with a distinct bright face and a dark edge, the warm amber light from the lower left keeping strictly to its own side while the cold cyan holds the rest, each colour staying purely itself in the same water.

A last few flakes after the storm: seven or eight soft white specks drift down at wide intervals, each one large and slow and distinct against the settled white rooftops below, the water itself gone still and faintly blue, every speck lit from behind by one low warm yellow source.

Snow rising: dozens of small white specks lift upward off a ridge of settled snow on the chapel roof, each one peeling away separately and floating up, backlit by a warm orange glow from the left so each rising speck glows briefly amber before the blue above swallows it.

One enormous slow flake near the glass: a single soft white speck the size of a thumbnail hangs close, edges ragged and gentle, drifting at the speed of a held breath, while behind it a haze of hundreds of fine specks recedes into deep cold indigo, the near speck lit warm ivory by the light.

One side of the water packed dense with white specks, each one tumbling fast, piling the view into pale opacity; the far side perfectly clear and deep cobalt blue, the world's rooftops sharp and terracotta-warm on that calm side, the storm edge cutting across the water like a weather front.

Warm ash instead of snow: hundreds of soft grey specks drift slowly downward, each one a separate feather-light scrap catching the deep orange firelight from below and glowing briefly rust before cooling to pale grey mid-fall, the water tinted a faint smoky amber near the heat source at the base.

Drifting pollen: thousands of individual specks, each one a tiny bright gold point, hang almost motionless through the full depth of the water, the light coming in from one side turning them each a saturated yellow-gold while the shadow side of the water stays deep forest green behind them.

Dandelion seeds drifting: each seed a separate white filament, maybe forty of them suspended at different heights, each one drifting so slowly it seems to choose its direction, the warm afternoon light catching each filament and turning it briefly luminous ivory against a background of deep amber-green water.

Cherry petals turning as they fall: sixty or seventy individual pink petals each tumbling with a slow roll as they descend, one edge catching the light and going pale rose, the other folding into deep magenta shadow, the water faintly pink-tinted near the base where petals have begun to settle in a soft drift.

Fine silt and bubbles through a reef: thousands of individual tan specks rise slowly upward while dozens of separate small bubbles each angle upward and slightly right, every bubble catching the bright turquoise light from above and holding a tiny pale highlight, the water warm green near the coral and deep teal above.

Grey moon dust: hundreds of individual pale grey specks hang perfectly suspended through the water with no drift at all, each one stationary at its own height, the cold white light from directly above pressing flat shadows beneath each speck, the water itself utterly still and a deep steel blue.

Rain: thousands of individual short bright streaks each angled the same direction, each one a separate white line no longer than a grain of rice, all slanting ten degrees from vertical, the cold blue-white light from above catching each streak along its top edge while the water below them stays deep grey-green.

Golden sparks lifting: hundreds of individual bright orange-gold specks each rising at slightly different speeds, the smallest ones near the top, the largest still near the heat at the base, each speck caught by the deep amber light below and glowing its own intense warm gold against a background of dark burgundy water.

Aurora light in the water: the water itself carries a faint suffused green tint that shifts to cold violet near the surface, and through it dozens of individual bright green specks drift slowly upward each one trailing a hair-thin wake, the light sourceless and even, turning the settled snow below a cold aquamarine.

Bubbles rising off-vertical: forty individual bubbles each rising in a line angled fifteen degrees from straight up, each bubble distinct and separate, each one catching the pale yellow light from one side and showing a bright point on its upper-left surface, the water a deep warm amber between them.

Sand drifting over a caravan: hundreds of individual warm brown specks each rolling slowly forward at the same low angle, the near ones large and distinct, the far ones a soft caramel haze, low amber light raking in from behind and catching the top surface of each speck in a brief intense orange before it moves on.

Confetti over a carnival: scraps of red, yellow and cobalt blue each tumbling separately through the water, no two the same angle, the bright warm light from the lanterns below catching the yellow scraps gold and the red ones a deep scarlet while the blue ones pass through shadow and go nearly violet.

Fireflies in the water: thirty-one individual warm yellow-white pinpoints each stationary for a long moment then drifting two or three millimetres before pausing again, each one a separate soft warm light source, the water between them deep green-black, the settled snow below lit from above by their collective warm ivory glow.

Soap-bubble iridescence: the water near one side has caught the light in such a way that thin interference colours — a stripe of pale gold, a stripe of thin blue — move slowly across the interior as the water shifts, while individual white specks pass through each colour and take it briefly before continuing their slow fall.

Snow with a tiny spin to it: every individual white speck in the water curves very slightly as it falls, each one tracing its own small arc rather than a straight line, the whole population of specks spiralling in the same lazy clockwise direction, the amber window-light catching each one at the peak of its outward arc.

Blizzard so thick the steeple dissolves: thousands upon thousands of individual white specks pack the water from surface to base, the farthest layer a solid pale opacity, only the nearest dozen specks individually visible and each one tumbling fast, the warm gold of the church windows bleeding into the surrounding white as diffuse amber haze.

Slow melt: dozens of individual white specks hang at mid-depth having stalled in their descent, each one softening at its edges and very slowly losing its hard white centre to a faint watery translucence, the warm light from below turning each softening speck briefly cream before the centre goes clear.

Storm edge passing: the right half of the water carries hundreds of dense individual white specks tumbling fast in a cold blue light, the left half nearly empty with only three or four isolated specks drifting free, the warm terracotta rooftops emerging clear and distinct on the left as the cold blue retreats rightward.

Fine green flecks of new leaf: hundreds of individual bright yellow-green specks drift downward very slowly, each one a separate soft point catching the warm spring-afternoon light and going a saturated lime-gold, while the water behind them grades from warm amber near the sunlit side to a rich deep jade in the shadow.

Snow settling in a long slow spiral around the steeple: each individual white speck orbits the steeple at a different height, the nearest ones large and slow, the farthest ones a fine pale haze, warm amber light from the windows below catching each speck at the bottom of its arc and cooling to blue at the top.

Full blizzard: thousands of individual white specks packed so dense the far side of the world is half-swallowed, each flake a separate soft tumbling point, cold blue light from above catching the nearest ones bright ivory while the deep water behind them goes dark cobalt.

A last handful of flakes after the storm — perhaps nine, perhaps twelve, each one a distinct slow-drifting speck with open dark water between them, warm amber light from the world's own lit windows catching each tiny white point and holding it gold before it settles.

Snow rising: dozens of individual white specks blown up off the rooftops and climbing, each one tilting as it lifts, warm ochre light from below catching their undersides pale gold while the upper water stays a cold deep slate blue.

One enormous slow flake hangs close to the front of the water, soft and irregular, every edge catching low warm light and glowing pale cream; behind it a loose haze of much finer separate specks recede into the water's deeper blue-green dark.

A whole left side of the water is packed with hundreds of individual white specks drifting densely together, the right side holding open dark teal space with only three or four lone flakes crossing it, warm side-light from the left turning the crowded specks bright white and leaving the far water cold.

Warm grey ash drifting down: each scrap a separate soft grey fleck, irregular and slow, some still dark at the edge, sinking through amber-lit water that turns the paler flecks warm ochre and lets the darker ones sink almost unlit into the deep brown shadow below.

Drifting pollen and dandelion seed: each filament a separate hair-fine golden speck, dozens of them hanging nearly still, low warm light from one side catching every individual thread and turning it bright amber-gold against the deep olive-green of the unlit water behind.

Cherry petals falling: each one a separate soft pink scrap turning slowly as it descends, the nearest one face-on and catching warm pink-white light, the ones behind it edge-on and almost invisible until they turn, the water itself a deep cool rose where the light passes through.

Fine silt and small bubbles rising through a reef: the silt a thousand individual pale tan specks drifting upward, each bubble a separate clear point catching turquoise light and throwing a tiny bright spot on the water just above it, the whole column angling slightly left.

Grey moon dust hanging: hundreds of individual pale grey specks suspended with almost no movement, each one a distinct mote, cold white light from above catching the uppermost layer stark and bright while the lower specks fade into deep charcoal shadow with no weather to shift them.

Rain: thousands of short individual bright streaks all angling the same way across the water, each streak a separate thin white-silver dash, cold blue-white light from above catching every one of them on the same edge and leaving the water between them a deep inky blue.

Golden sparks lifting off a bonfire: each spark a separate warm amber point rising unevenly, some climbing fast, some drifting sideways, low orange light from below catching the nearest ones copper-bright while the higher ones cool to pale gold against the deep black of the upper water.

Bright green flecks of aurora light adrift in the water itself: each one a separate soft green mote, slow and unhurried, cold deep violet in the surrounding water making each individual green speck read sharp, the lowest ones yellowing slightly as they near the warmer amber sediment below.

Bubbles rising in a long tilted line, each one a separate clear point, each chasing the one above it and angling off to the right, cold blue light from the side catching the left edge of each bubble bright white and leaving the right edge a deep cool shadow.

Sand, warm and brown, drifting in slow low waves over a desert caravan: each grain a separate tiny amber speck moving together with the current but each one distinct at the front edge of the drift, warm side-light from the right turning the leading grains bright burnt sienna and the trailing ones deep shadow-brown.

Confetti over a carnival: each scrap a separate bright irregular fragment — one red, one yellow, one deep blue tumbling past it — all falling at slightly different speeds, warm white light from below catching the nearest scraps vivid and flat while the ones behind flutter edge-on into the darker water.

Fireflies instead of flakes: each one a separate small warm point of soft yellow-white light moving at its own unhurried pace, some rising, some drifting sideways, the water between them a deep summer-night green, the nearest firefly close enough that its warm glow touches the water just around it amber.

Soap-bubble iridescence where the light enters the water: not the flakes but the water itself showing faint thin interference colour — pale violet on one band, pale copper on the next — each colour shift a separate thin wash across different depths, the flakes drifting through them picking up first one colour then the other.

Snow with a tiny spin still in it, as though the whole world was set down moments ago: dozens of individual white specks still curving gently in a slow clockwise drift, each one tracing its own small arc, warm amber light from one side catching them on the upswing bright cream and losing them on the downswing into cool blue shadow.

Blizzard so thick the nearest specks are large distinct white points and the middle distance is a close crowd of smaller separate specks and beyond them the far side of the world is only a soft pale smear, cold blue light catching the front layer stark while everything behind grades deeper and deeper into blue-black.

A single side of the water packed thick: on the right, hundreds of individual white specks so close together their separate edges nearly touch, the water there a pale grey-white mass of distinct points; on the left, open deep teal with five solitary specks crossing the empty space, warm light from the right side turning the dense crowd bright and leaving the open side cool.

Warm ash after a long burn: each fleck a soft dark grey scrap, some still showing a pale cream edge where they haven't fully cooled, drifting down slowly and unevenly through amber-lit water, the deepest ones settling into a thin soft layer of warm ochre sediment already accumulating low down.

Cherry petals mid-gust: each petal a separate pale pink scrap tilted at the same steep angle, all of them slanting hard to the left as though the whole world leans into a warm spring wind, low warm light from the left catching the leading face of each petal bright rose-white and leaving the trailing edge deep mauve shadow.

Fine individual specks of pollen, each one a separate rounded yellow-green mote, drifting very slowly downward and slightly sideways, a long warm light from the lower right catching each mote and turning it a different shade — the nearest ones bright gold, the farther ones a cooler yellow-green — against deep blue-green water.

The very end of a blizzard: most flakes already settled into a thick soft white layer low down, but a dozen separate individual specks still drifting in the open water above, each one moving at its own slow pace in slightly different directions as the storm's last energy fades, warm amber window-light from the world below catching them soft gold against the darkening blue above.

The storm is nearly spent — four, maybe five separate soft white flakes still drifting, each one large enough to track individually as it tilts and descends, settling onto a rooftop already blanketed deep, the surrounding water gone still and faintly dark indigo in the quiet aftermath.

Snow rising: dozens of individual white specks lifted off the ridge of a steep roof, each one peeling away separately and climbing on a slow diagonal, the low amber light from behind catching their undersides bright while the cold blue overhead turns each tumbling one pale silver the moment it clears the eave.

One enormous soft white flake hangs close, nearly pressed to the inside surface — its every branching arm softly visible and trembling — while behind it, a fine haze of much smaller specks recedes in layers into the deep blue-green water toward the far steeple.

The left half of the water is thick with individual white specks, each one faintly amber-lit from the left, packed closely enough to grey out the street and tower behind them, while the right half of the water is open and dark teal, the buildings there standing sharp and unweathed.

Warm grey ash: hundreds of individual soft grey flecks drifting slowly downward on a gentle lean, each one flat and slow-turning, the low russet light from a fire somewhere off to the side catching the top face of each fleck copper-warm while the undersides remain cool and dark.

Gold and cream: dozens of individual dandelion seeds drift at different heights through amber-lit water, each one a tiny puff of threads distinct from the next, a few snagged briefly against the carved lintel of a doorway before the slow water pulls them off and down again.

Cherry petals: each one a separate blush-pink scrap turning lazily on its own axis as it descends, the warm golden light from below catching the pale inner face of each upturned petal and making it glow briefly apricot before it rolls face-down and goes cool and deep rose.

Fine silt and tiny bubbles rising through deep reef water — each bubble a clear rising point catching the turquoise overhead light and throwing a tiny bright patch on the coral face it passes — while below, each grain of silt drifts across the sandy floor in the warm amber of shallow tropical sun.

Moon dust: hundreds of individual grey-white particles hang perfectly motionless at every depth, none settling, none rising, the cold silver light from directly above touching the top of each particle so each one is lit on one face and dark on the other, the whole water utterly still.

Rain: thousands of individual short bright streaks, each one white on its leading edge and pale blue-grey along its length, all slanting the same way at the same angle as though the whole water has a shared wind, the deep water behind them a saturated cobalt between strikes.

Golden sparks: individual bright amber specks rising through dark water in loose separate clusters, each one climbing at its own pace and flickering as it turns in the water, the lowest ones just leaving the smudge of a warm orange fire visible low down, the highest ones cooling to a faint ember-red as they rise.

Bright green flecks suspended at mid-water, each one a separate vivid mint-green point, some hanging still, some very slowly drifting sideways, the cold blue light from above turning the water between them a deep peacock blue while each green fleck holds its own warm colour against the dark.

Bubbles rising in a long loose angled line, each one separate and clear, each climbing on a slight lean off true vertical so the whole sequence tilts away from the nearest building like something underground is breathing out slowly, the teal overhead light sliding across each rising bubble in turn.

Warm brown sand grains drifting low, each individual speck rolling and skipping just above the curve of dune-ground in the slow water, the amber afternoon light from one side catching the face of each grain amber-gold while the far side of the dune lies in deep burnt-sienna shadow.

Confetti: each scrap a separate bright fragment — scarlet, cobalt, chrome yellow — tumbling independently through the water, some spinning fast, some barely turning, the warm golden carnival light below catching the underside of each upward-facing scrap and making the colours deeper and hotter than they'd be in air.

Individual warm amber firefly-points, each one a separate soft glow rising through the dark water on its own slow upward wander, the deep water between them a saturated forest green, each point brightening very slightly as it reaches the warmest layer of water near the top before going out.

Soap-film iridescence where the light enters from the left — thin petrol-blue and bronze interference colours sliding slowly across the near face of the water as the angle of each tiny suspended droplet shifts, the far side of the water staying a clean dark sapphire untouched by the colour play.

Snow with a faint residual spin — each individual white speck still curving very slightly as it falls rather than dropping straight, the whole population of flakes describing a loose shared spiral around the steeple as though the world was only just set down, the warm amber window-light catching each speck on the inside of its arc.

A mid-blizzard gust caught mid-action: the specks on the left are moving fast and tilted steeply, each one a short bright white streak, while those on the sheltered right side of the water are still nearly round and slow, the cobalt blue cold light from above splitting the water cleanly between the two behaviours.

The last three individual white flakes of a spent storm, each one large and very slow, widely separated in the deep still water, each casting a faint shadow down through the water below it in the warm amber window-light, the settled snow below catching that amber and sending it back up pale gold.

Fine white specks lifting off a snow-covered plaza in a slow upward drift — each one peeling off the surface separately rather than together — rising through cold blue-lit water while below them the settled surface they've left holds a faint amber warmth from the lit arcade along its edge.

A dense population of individual white specks occupies the top two-thirds of the water, each one softly visible, while the lowest third is almost clear — the specks still descending toward that clear zone but not yet there, so the boundary between crowd and open water is ragged and slowly advancing, lit warm amber from behind.

Individual ice-pale specks all tilted the same way as though the whole world leans slightly right, every flake a separate point slanting on the same diagonal through deep cold teal water, the single warm orange light from a low window on the right edge back-lighting every passing speck to a brief bright white before the dark closes in behind it.

Pollen: each grain a separate tiny deep-gold speck drifting at mid-height through still water, some clumped in loose neighbourhoods of three or four, some solitary, the warm amber light from below turning the water between them a rich honey colour while the upper water above the pollen layer stays a clear and cooler pale green.

Last few flakes after the storm: one large soft speck descends close to the glass, moving with the patient gravity of something that has been falling a long time, while three or four fine distant specks hang almost motionless far behind it. Warm amber light from a lit window inside the world throws a small halo into the surrounding water and catches the near flake from the side, edging it gold against the deep cold blue of the settled, heavy water below.
